text.tspan: : Lower confidence corresponds to narrower intervals.
So, if we want to have a small margin of error, we have two options.
Often, this is a trade-off. Sometimes we would like to be 99% confident in our interval, but it will
require too much data. So, we accept 95%, or 90% to get the margin of error down. Other times, data is
easy to obtain, so we can decrease the error by simply collecting more observations. See
: Large sample size and lower confidence lead to
smaller margins of error and narrower intervals.
